Medical History

- Current health issues and chronic disease risk factors (e.g., hypertension, diabetes):  Acute 3-day history of diarrhea with urgency/tenesmus, infra-umbilical abdominal pain with borborygmi, and one episode of vomiting after fruit; no visible blood in stool; uncertain fever (reports sweating, not sure about temperature); mild abdominal tenderness on self-palpation. Known asthma; uses inhaler. Hydration likely suboptimal per patient report.  
- Family history of chronic conditions (e.g., CVD, diabetes):  Father died of bowel (colorectal) cancer ~10 years ago.  
- Current medications including OTC and traditional medicines:  Asthma inhaler (recent brand change; dose/route/frequency not documented).  
- Immunisation status reviewed (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus):  Not recorded.  
- Sexual/reproductive health status and risks:  Not recorded.  
- Lifestyle: physical activity, diet, tobacco, alcohol, substance use:  Employed; currently staying home due to symptoms. Eating less to avoid frequent stools. Fluid intake likely low. Tobacco, alcohol, and other substances not recorded.

- Mood, mental health, and risk assessment (depression, anxiety, self-harm):  Reports anxiety at times; uses inhaler when anxious. No self-harm reported.

Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

- Summary of key clinical findings: Acute, self-limited course of diarrhea (3 days) with infra-umbilical crampy pain and urgency; one emesis; no visible blood; uncertain fever; mild abdominal tenderness; likely dehydration; history of asthma with recent inhaler brand change; significant family history of colorectal cancer (father).  
- Working diagnosis: Acute viral gastroenteritis. Supported by acute onset, crampy abdominal pain with borborygmi, nausea/vomiting, frequent loose stools without blood or high fever (DDx concurs: “High” likelihood).  
- Considerations (from DDx, consistent with transcript):  
  - Acute bacterial gastroenteritis/foodborne illness (Medium): Overlapping presentation; absence of blood/high fever lowers likelihood.  
  - IBS-D (Low–Medium): Pain relief after defecation and urgency could fit, but acute course argues against.  
  - Inflammatory bowel disease (Low) and colorectal cancer (Low): Family history raises baseline cancer risk, but acute, short duration without bleeding or weight loss argues against as cause of current illness.  
- Plan:  
  - Supportive care: Increase fluids (oral hydration) given ongoing losses.  
  - Observation for fever/clinical deterioration.  
  - Stay home until improving.  
  - Antibiotics not indicated at this time (may worsen course per clinician advice).  
  - Safety net: If symptoms worsen or fail to improve, attend in-person GP assessment for abdominal examination.  
  - Asthma: No current worsening of breathing; inhaler brand change unlikely cause of GI symptoms. Continue usual inhaler use as needed.  

Health Promotion & Planning

- Education on chronic disease prevention and lifestyle modification:  Discussed supportive care for gastroenteritis (fluids) and to avoid unnecessary antibiotics for presumed viral illness.  
- Patient health goals and priorities:  Plans to monitor for 1–2 days; will book in-person GP if not improving.  
- Eligibility for GP Management Plan (GPMP) or Team Care Arrangements (TCA):  Not recorded.

- Follow-up and recall appointments scheduled:  Patient to arrange in-person GP visit in 1–2 days if not improved or sooner if worsening.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx)

- Acute viral gastroenteritis — High likelihood: Acute 3-day course of crampy midline abdominal pain, nausea/vomiting, and frequent loose stools without blood or high fever.  
- Acute bacterial gastroenteritis (foodborne) — Medium likelihood: Infectious colitis can present similarly; lack of blood/high fever lowers probability.  
- Irritable bowel syndrome, diarrhea-predominant (IBS-D) — Low–Medium likelihood: Pain relief after defecation and urgency align, but acute onset and associated vomiting favor infection over functional disorder.  

Quality checks

- Missing but clinically expected elements: No vitals, BMI, or physical exam recorded; no urinalysis; immunization review (flu, COVID-19, pneumococcal, shingles, tetanus) not done; no chronic disease screening reviewed (lipids, glucose/HbA1c); no cancer screening reviewed (FOBT/colorectal screening, cervical, mammography); no renal/liver tests.  
- Internal conflicts or contradictions: Assessment template is for adults 55+; patient age reported as 48 (conflict noted). Patient stated “I have NKDA allergy,” interpreted as no known drug allergies; phrasing atypical but consistent with DDx.  
- Transcript quality notes: Telehealth encounter with incomplete history (no travel/sick contacts/antibiotic exposure documented); patient uncertain about fever; some dialogue unclear/elliptical.
